_comment: Conventional Commits → a version bump, a tag, and a GitHub Release.
── One package, one version
zoning ships one crate (`crates/zoning`) and its PyPI wheel envelope, the
same binary in two package managers. `Cargo.toml`'s `[workspace.package]
version` is the single source of truth — `crates/zoning/Cargo.toml`
inherits it via `version.workspace = true`, and `pyproject.toml` declares
`dynamic = ["version"]` so maturin reads it straight from Cargo at build
time. Neither is a second mirror to move.
── Why `simple` + generic extra-files
`simple` keeps the manifest as the source of truth; the `generic` updater
rewrites the semver on any line carrying an `x-release-please-version`
annotation — one line, in this repo. The shared `package-release version`
command fails if that marked line is missing from this list, so the two
cannot drift apart. `editors/vscode/package.json` is a second mirror —
the VSIX manifest version, which `editors/vscode/scripts/validate.mjs`
asserts still equals Cargo.toml's — bumped through the `json` updater
(JSONPath, not an annotation, since JSON has no comment syntax) so a
release can never advance one and forget the other.
── Changelog ownership
towncrier owns CHANGELOG.md — the curated fragments under changelog.d/ are
the release notes, written for people. release-please would compile a
second, machine-derived changelog into the same file and fight it, so
`skip-changelog` is on and the bot handles versions and tags only. The
`fold changelog` job in release-please.yml builds the notes and commits
them onto this PR's branch automatically; release.yml's preflight
re-checks that the fold landed before it will publish anything.
── What picks the number
The stock `default` versioning strategy, which is plain semver over the
commit types: a `!` or a BREAKING CHANGE footer takes the major, `feat`
takes the minor, and EVERYTHING ELSE takes the patch. There is no setting
here pushing releases toward minors — a window whose commits are all
`fix`/`perf`/`refactor`/`ci` cuts a patch, and the only reason this repo
had not cut one before 1.3 is that every window so far happened to carry
exactly one `feat`.
`bump-minor-pre-major` and `bump-patch-for-minor-pre-major` used to sit
here and are gone: release-please reads them only while the version is
below 1.0.0, so they stopped meaning anything at 1.0.0 and stayed on as
config that looked like a bump policy. Re-add them only if something here
ever ships a 0.x again.
To pin an exact number instead — a patch on a minor nobody cut, a version
skipped to line up with a consumer — put `Release-As: X.Y.Z` in a commit
body on main. The newest one found wins and overrides everything above.
── The tag cascades
Merging the release PR tags `vX.Y.Z`, which is what `release.yml` waits
for to publish the wheels and the crate. A tag pushed by GITHUB_TOKEN does
NOT trigger another workflow, so that hand-off only happens because
release-please runs as the `billy-company-release` GitHub App rather than
as Actions — see .github/workflows/release-please.yml.
